args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and find out why it was promoted even though the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, was failing health checks and had an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is now running in all three regions. After the rollback, the service passes health checks and the error rate is down to about 0.2%. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 was healthy in production before.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the results afterwards. It lists two next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and find out why it was promoted even though the release candidate was unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
